title: Initiating: project initiation and kickoff workshops
blurb: Explain the initiating activities in agile terms and sort topics between the project initiation workshop and the project kickoff workshop.
question: During initiation, one workshop defines a project Definition of Ready and personas, while another builds a skill matrix and team dashboards. Which workshops are these?

teach.body: Initiating a project lays solid foundations so the business understands the work needed before committing significant expenditure or resources. In agile terms that means agreeing tailoring and management approaches, setting controls, documenting the release map and refining the project canvas. Two workshops support it: the project initiation workshop and the project kickoff workshop. As in starting up, the PM defines the participants, sets the dates and sends the invitations.

head: Activity
What happens
rows: Seek tailoring lessons; record them in the PID
Change, communication, sustainability, benefits, commercial, quality, risk, issue, digital and data
Stage boundaries, project tolerances, escalation and decision rules
Update the project backlog if needed; plan transition; document the release map
Cross-check its parts; baseline the version used for authorization
Share final canvas, PID and release map with the board
teach.caption: Paraphrased from Table 13.6; 'assemble the PID' follows PRINCE2 7 (manual 15.4.6).

teach.body: Its purpose is to align on the vision and objectives, develop a high-level release map and set up structured yet flexible management approaches. Everyone assesses the Agilometer and the scores are combined into one project Agilometer. The group co-creates the approaches (replacing the change management approach with an agile transformation plan if needed), defines the project DoR and DoD and personas, plans releases and refines the canvas.

head: Topic
Typical output
rows: Criteria to start work on user stories
Criteria for work acceptable to users/CPO
Canvas aligned with the release map
teach.caption: Table 13.7, paraphrased.

teach.body: The kickoff aligns the team and stakeholders on vision, objectives and scope, builds teamwork and creates an agile culture of openness and self-management. Topics run from an icebreaker with project and team introductions, through a psychological safety assessment, team values and norms, a team skill matrix and a team delegation matrix, to team dashboards co-created by each team and the project dashboard, which is created here.

steps.label: Dashboards
steps.sub: team ones co-created; project one created

teach.body: At Tidewell Logistics, project manager Sofia Marin runs the project initiation workshop for a driver scheduling app. Everyone scores the Agilometer, the group agrees that stories need clear acceptance criteria before work starts (project DoR), CPO James Okafor leads persona writing, and the release map is updated. At the kickoff a week later, team coach Lena Fischer helps each team agree values, fill in a skill matrix and design its own team dashboard.

teach.text: Team dashboards are co-created by each team in the kickoff, NOT dictated by the project manager. Criteria for starting work belong to the project Definition of Ready topic, not 'management approaches'. The project dashboard is created in the kickoff workshop, not in starting up.

items: Initiating: solid foundations before significant expenditure.
Activities: tailoring, approaches, controls, project plan (release map), full business case (canvas), assemble the PID, request authorization.
Initiation workshop: Agilometer, approaches, project DoR and DoD, personas, release planning, canvas refinement.
Agile transformation plan can replace the change management approach (initiation workshop).
Kickoff: intros, psychological safety, values and norms, skill and delegation matrices, dashboards.
Team dashboards are co-created; the project dashboard is created at kickoff.

summary: You can now describe initiating a project in agile terms and place each topic in the project initiation workshop or the project kickoff workshop. You also know which artifacts each workshop produces.

A.q: Which topic of the project initiation workshop lists product-overarching criteria that must be met before work on user stories can start?
A.why: The project Definition of Ready topic sets criteria needed before work can be handed to development (Table 13.7).

whyNot.1: The project DoD sets criteria for work to be acceptable to users or the CPO, at the end.
whyNot.2: Management approaches covers overarching governance such as risk and quality, not readiness criteria.
whyNot.3: Persona definition describes key users to guide product decisions.

A.q: Which topic of the project kickoff workshop maps each team member's skills and identifies gaps or overlaps?
A.why: The team skill matrix maps skills and shows gaps and overlaps (Table 13.8).

whyNot.0: Values and norms build an agile culture and manage expectations.
whyNot.1: The delegation matrix simplifies decisions and empowers self-management.
whyNot.3: Team dashboards give transparency on team progress.

A.q: In which initiating activity does the PM document the release map and identify arrangements for moving the product into operational use?
A.why: Prepare the project plan updates the project backlog if needed, plans the transition to operations, confirms resources and documents the release map (Table 13.6).

whyNot.0: Project controls cover stage boundaries, tolerances and escalation.
whyNot.1: This activity defines the nine management approaches.
whyNot.2: The full business case is a more detailed project canvas.

B.q: What is the purpose of the project kickoff workshop?
options: To co-create management approaches and the project DoR
To align team and stakeholders and build teamwork
To confirm the outline business case with the executive
To review Agilometer results with the project board
B.why: The kickoff aligns the team and stakeholders on vision, objectives and scope and builds a foundation for teamwork and self-management (13.4.4.2).

whyNot.0: Approaches and the project DoR are project initiation workshop topics.
whyNot.2: The outline business case is prepared in starting up.
whyNot.3: Reviewing the Agilometer with the board is the agile enablement workshop.

B.q: Which initiating activity confirms the stage boundaries, project tolerances and escalation and decision-making procedures?
B.why: Establish project controls documents stage boundaries, tolerances and escalation procedures (Table 13.6).

whyNot.0: Tailoring requirements are recorded in the PID in a separate activity.
whyNot.1: The project plan activity documents the release map.
whyNot.2: Requesting authorization shares the canvas, PID and release map with the board.

B.q: Which project initiation workshop topic co-creates the management approaches and may replace the change management approach with an agile transformation plan?
B.why: The management approaches topic co-creates approaches for structured agility; if needed the change management approach is replaced by an agile transformation plan (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: Canvas refinement aligns the canvas with the updated release map.
whyNot.1: Release planning updates the high-level release map.
whyNot.3: The Agilometer topic combines everyone's assessments into one project Agilometer.

C.q: At the kickoff, a project manager tells every team exactly what its team dashboard must show. Which statement is correct?
options: It conflicts with the kickoff aim of openness and self-management
It is correct, as the PM owns all dashboards during initiation
It belongs in the project Definition of Done topic instead
It is correct, as team dashboards replace highlight reports
C.why: Team dashboards are co-created by each team; dictating them contradicts the kickoff's aim of openness and self-management (13.4.4.2, Table 13.8).

whyNot.1: Team dashboards belong to the teams that co-create them.
whyNot.2: The project DoD sets acceptance criteria for work, not dashboard design.
whyNot.3: Team dashboards replace checkpoint reports; the project dashboard replaces highlight reports.

C.q:
Which two statements about initiating a project are correct?
1. 'Prepare the full business case' produces a more detailed project canvas.
2. Persona definition is a project kickoff workshop topic.
3. In the project initiation workshop, individual Agilometer assessments are combined into one.
4. The team delegation matrix is a project initiation workshop topic.
C.why: The full business case is a more detailed project canvas (Table 13.6), and individual Agilometer assessments are combined into one project Agilometer (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: personas belong to the project initiation workshop.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: personas are an initiation workshop topic and the delegation matrix a kickoff topic.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: the delegation matrix is a kickoff topic.

C.q: Which initiating activity shares the final project canvas, PID and release map with the board, and which directing activity responds to it?
options: Establish project controls; give ongoing direction
Prepare the project plan; authorize a stage
Request project authorization; authorize the project
C.why: The PM requests project authorization (Table 13.6) and the board responds in 'authorize the project', approving the PID (Table 13.4).

whyNot.0: Authorize initiation comes before initiation, approving the brief.
whyNot.1: Controls set tolerances; ongoing direction is informal advice.
whyNot.2: The project plan activity documents the release map; stage authorization follows later stages.

reteach.title: Moving into a new shared house
reteach.question: How do the two initiation workshops look when friends move into a shared house?

blocks.body: First the housemates agree how the house will run: what 'clean' means before you cook (ready) and after you cook (done), who the house is really for, and a rough plan for the first months. That is the initiation workshop. Then they get to know each other: what each person is good at, who decides what, how they will show who has done which chores. That is the kickoff.

blocks.text: Each room designs its own chore board; nobody imposes it. Team dashboards are co-created, not dictated.

explain.body: Initiation agrees nine management approaches: change, communication, sustainability, benefits, commercial, quality, risk, issue, and digital and data. If an agile transformation is involved, an agile transformation plan can replace the change management approach.

test.q: If needed, which management approach can be replaced by an agile transformation plan?
test.why: The project initiation workshop may replace the change management approach with an agile transformation plan (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: Communication stays as its own approach, bidirectional and tailored.
whyNot.1: Benefits management stays within the business case practice.
whyNot.3: Quality management stays and includes agile ways of working.

explain.body: The project initiation workshop combines the Agilometer, approaches, project DoR and DoD, personas, high-level release planning and canvas refinement.

test.q: Which project initiation workshop topic identifies key user personas to guide product decisions?
test.why: Persona definition identifies and defines key user personas (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: Canvas refinement aligns the canvas with the release map.
whyNot.2: Release planning updates the release map.
whyNot.3: The project DoD sets acceptance criteria.

explain.body: The skill matrix shows skills, gaps and overlaps; the delegation matrix makes decision rights clear so teams can self-manage.

test.q: Which kickoff topic aims to simplify decision-making and empower self-management?
test.why: The team delegation matrix simplifies decisions and empowers self-management (Table 13.8).

whyNot.1: Values and norms build culture and expectations.
whyNot.2: Psychological safety is assessed to support open contribution.
whyNot.3: The skill matrix maps skills, gaps and overlaps.

explain.body: In the kickoff, each team co-creates its team dashboard for transparency and quick insight, and the project dashboard is created for the board to pull information.

test.q: In which workshop is the project dashboard created?
test.why: The project dashboard is created in the project kickoff workshop (Table 13.8).

whyNot.0: The starting up workshop creates the project backlog with epics and updates the release map.
whyNot.1: The agile enablement workshop reviews agile risks with the board.
whyNot.3: The progress review reviews project dashboard metrics; it does not create the dashboard.
